transcript:
alex (PM): quick sync — need to lock Optimize toolkit priorities for next sprint. main candidates: quantization profiles, smart batching controls, prefix/KV caching enhancements. thinking we should pick ordering now so eng can scope.

sanjay (Eng): +1. can we use RICE to make this objective? I can sketch rough scores.

lena (ML): yes please. also call out launch criteria: regression <1% on quality evals, <20% token cost reduction targets, and no latency tail >95th 2x baseline.

yara (Customer Success): customer asks: 3 enterprise customers requested per-route caching and deterministic quant profiles — high ARR signal. one asked for per-tenant rollback.

mike (Data): we have evals for quant at 3 bits vs 4 bits on our Llama-variant. quality drop at 3-bit is 2.7% on QA set; 4-bit is 0.9%. cost savings: 3-bit ~35%, 4-bit ~20%.

sanjay (Eng): rough effort estimates (very rough): quant profiles = 6w (model work + infra + canary), batching controls (config + runtime) = 3w, KV/prefix caching (hot path + invalidation) = 5w.

alex (PM): cool. @lena @mike can you drop R/I/C/E numbers? I'll compute RICE.

lena (ML): impact estimates (0-10): quantization = 7 (good cost wins but risk), batching = 5 (improves throughput for high-concurrency customers), caching = 8 (big wins for request patterns we see). confidence (0-10): quant 6, batch 8, cache 7. reach (users affected): quant 60%, batching 40%, cache 55%. effort in person-weeks: quant 24, batch 12, cache 20.

alex (PM): i'm pasting an inline table so we can eyeball RICE quickly:

```
Feature | Reach (%) | Impact (0-10) | Confidence (0-10) | Effort (pw)
quantization | 60 | 7 | 6 | 24
batching controls | 40 | 5 | 8 | 12
prefix/KV caching | 55 | 8 | 7 | 20
```

sanjay (Eng): calculating RICE = (Reach*Impact*Confidence)/Effort (normalize reach to fraction). I ran numbers quickly:

- quantization: (0.6*7*6)/24 = 1.05
- batching: (0.4*5*8)/12 = 1.33
- caching: (0.55*8*7)/20 = 1.54

so ordering by RICE -> caching, batching, quantization.

yara (Customer Success): that tracks with customer asks — caching keeps popping up. but quantization is strategic for unit economics at scale. any middle ground?

lena (ML): we can scope quant as phased: start with 4-bit standard profile (lower risk, 0.9% QA drop) and treat 3-bit as experimental opt-in. that reduces rollout risk and effort for initial launch.

sanjay (Eng): good call. that could reduce effort to ~16 pw for the initial quant MVP (4-bit plus conservative monitors).

alex (PM): propose prioritization/sequence: 1) prefix/KV caching (ship MVP with invalidation + metrics), 2) batching controls (expose batch timeout/batch size heuristics + autosuggest), 3) quantization phased (4-bit default opt-in, 3-bit behind feature flag + canary).

mike (Data): launch criteria for each: caching = 10% median token cost reduction in our top 10 workloads OR 20% hit rate on cache; batching = 15% throughput increase for bursty endpoints w/out >10% latency tail regression; quant 4-bit = <1% quality drop on evals and >15% cost reduction on typical sequences.

alex (PM): tradeoffs to note in the roadmap doc: caching introduces cache invalidation complexity (customer-specific prompts), batching has hard realtime constraints for low-latency routes, quant requires careful per-model calibration + extra evals. we'll capture mitigations.

yara (Customer Success): for enterprise asks, we should add rollout options: per-tenant toggles, audit logs, and rollback path. if caching is first, make sure per-route toggles are in scope.

sanjay (Eng): agree. also need to budget SRE time for observability dashboards and 95th/99th tail alarms.

alex (PM): action items:
- @sanjay: produce high-level implementation plan + exact PW breakdown for caching and batching by EOD Tue
- @lena & @mike: finalize quant evals for 4-bit vs 3-bit and confirm launch thresholds by Wed
- @yara: gather top-5 customer asks and priority for per-tenant controls by Wed

sanjay (Eng): noted. will add dependency on rollout toggles and metrics.

lena (ML): i'll also propose a simple AB evaluation harness for quant rollout so we can monitor regressions live.

mike (Data): i'll prepare an analysis notebook and link it in the roadmap doc.

alex (PM): thanks all — let's reconvene Thu morning for final sign-off. :thumbsup:
